tagline: Australia's cultural capital pairs famous coffee and laneway street art with world-class sport, great food and easy day trips along the Great Ocean Road. It is ranked #1 on Time Out's Best Cities 2026 list.
overview: Founded in 1835 on the banks of the Yarra River, Melbourne boomed during the 1850s gold rush, when it was briefly one of the richest cities in the world. The grand Victorian-era buildings, boulevards and tram network date from that era.

The city centre hides its best bits in laneways: tiny coffee bars, street art on Hosier Lane, indie shops and rooftop bars. Melbourne is often credited with kicking off the global flat white craze, and the coffee obsession here is serious business.

Sport is close to a religion. The Melbourne Cricket Ground holds around 100,000 fans, and the city hosts the Australian Open, the Formula 1 Grand Prix and the AFL Grand Final. For day trips, the Twelve Apostles on the Great Ocean Road and the penguin parade on Phillip Island are favourites.

funFacts.title: CAPITAL OF AUSTRALIA... FOR A WHILE
funFacts.text: Melbourne served as Australia's capital from 1901 until Canberra took over in 1927.

funFacts.title: THE WORLD'S LARGEST TRAM NETWORK
funFacts.text: Melbourne's trams cover around 250 kilometres of track, the largest operating tram network in the world.

funFacts.title: A GOLD RUSH BOOMTOWN
funFacts.text: During the 1850s gold rush, Melbourne was briefly one of the richest cities on Earth, earning the nickname 'Marvellous Melbourne'.

funFacts.title: A COFFEE CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Melbourne claims a role in popularising the flat white, now on coffee menus around the world.

funFacts.title: HOME OF AUSSIE RULES
funFacts.text: Australian rules football was invented in Melbourne in 1858, and the AFL Grand Final fills the roughly 100,000-seat MCG.

funFacts.title: FIRST SOUTHERN OLYMPICS
funFacts.text: Melbourne was the first city in the southern hemisphere to host the Olympic Games, in 1956.

funFacts.title: HIDDEN BARS
funFacts.text: Many of Melbourne's best bars hide on rooftops and down laneways behind unmarked doors.

funFacts.title: PENGUINS NEARBY
funFacts.text: Every sunset, little penguins waddle ashore at Phillip Island, about 90 minutes from the city.

funFacts.title: FOUR SEASONS IN ONE DAY
funFacts.text: Locals joke you can experience all four seasons in a single day thanks to the fast-changing weather.

funFacts.title: THE SKYDECK
funFacts.text: The Eureka Tower's 88th-floor observation deck was the highest public vantage point in the southern hemisphere when it opened.
